Crunchtime will not see it as on order: An order you say in our app is not a Crunchtime vendor order. If Crunchtime's recommended amounts subtract what is already on order, they will not know about this delivery. Until it arrives, allow for it by hand when you read the next suggestion. When it comes in, record it in Crunchtime yourself, or get help from whoever set up your Crunchtime account.

Switch off auto-order for that distributor: If Crunchtime auto-orders from that distributor, auto-order has to be turned off for them before your first spoken order, so they get one order, not two. Ask whoever runs your Crunchtime setup, or do it yourself if that is you.

Begin with the vendor you already call: When Crunchtime's setup says to phone a vendor, it sends that vendor nothing, so getting that order to the distributor is already up to you. That order is the easiest one to move into our app, unless your brand wants it kept in Crunchtime.

@graph.name: Do I need a Crunchtime alternative to order from my local distributor by voice?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Crunchtime keeps doing your counts and forecasts, and keeps ordering from the vendors it is linked with. If your distributor is on VoiceOrder Solutions, you can order from them by voice in our app, with no call to the rep. A small supplier may not have it yet: ask them, or contact us to find out.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Crunchtime?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not at what Crunchtime does: we run no counts, forecasts, labor schedules or kitchen screens. Our app is for ordering from a distributor who has signed up with us: you say what you need, then look over every item before it is sent. If one supplier with no Crunchtime link is why you went looking for a Crunchtime alternative, that is the order our app can take.

@graph.name: Do VoiceOrder Solutions and Crunchtime connect?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We answer questions about our app, Crunchtime answers questions about theirs, and neither team supports the other's product. Whatever you order with us goes only to your distributor; Crunchtime never gets a copy.

@graph.name: Is this the same as Crunchtime's voice counts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Crunchtime's Voice-Based Inventory, an add-on for its Inventory app, lets you count aloud: say an item and an amount. Our app turns what you say into order lines, then sends them to the distributor who gave you the app. You can use both: Crunchtime for the count, our app for the order.

@graph.name: Can I order commissary items or transfers this way?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Both stay in Crunchtime. We handle orders to distributors that use VoiceOrder Solutions, nothing else.

@graph.name: I said two cases and the app shows six. What now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing has gone yet, so fix it on the review screen: change the amount, swap the item or delete the line. That review is the safeguard, and a hurried look can still miss a mistake. A call or a voicemail gets no number from us; only app orders do.

@graph.name: How do I get set up, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Through your distributor: they set up your account with your order guide, and most kitchens place a first order in the app that same day. If they do not have it, your orders to them stay as they are today. Contact us and we will connect you with the right person. VoiceOrder Solutions comes to you from your distributor, so cost is a question for them; we publish no price. Crunchtime's own site does not list its prices.

@graph.name: Where do the Crunchtime details on this page come from?

If you find a detail that is now wrong, email us and we will correct it.
